Title: US allegedly preparing UAV strikes in Nigeria as covert ISR flights reported - Businessday NG

Summary: 
Allegations have emerged that the United States is conducting covert intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) flights over Nigeria, with claims from Sahel terrorism tracker Brant Philip stating that a manned U.S. ISR aircraft flew over Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) strongholds near Lake Chad in Borno State on Saturday, originating from Accra, Ghana. Philip reported the same aircraft conducted a third consecutive day of reconnaissance over ISWAP’s 'Mantiqah Krinwa' enclave by Sunday. These reports follow earlier claims—also attributed to an unnamed source—that the U.S. is preparing unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) strikes inside Nigeria under a new, undisclosed security arrangement, allowing only drones for kinetic operations and excluding manned fighter jets or bombers. The U.S. military’s role, according to the source, would focus on closing intelligence gaps for Nigerian forces, potentially using Kainji Air Base in Niger State as a launch site. Philip further alleged that the U.S. Department of Defence (referred to as the 'Department of War') has begun reconnaissance missions from military facilities in Ghana, entering Nigerian airspace without public disclosure. The claims prompted backlash, with former presidential aide Bashir Ahmad accusing Philip of endangering operations by revealing sensitive details. The controversy coincided with high-level talks between U.S. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth and Nigeria’s National Security Adviser Mallam Nuhu Ribadu in Washington over terrorist threats and attacks on Christian communities. Despite mounting speculation, both the Nigerian and U.S. governments have not confirmed or denied the presence of ISR flights or UAV strike preparations. Nigeria continues to face a surge in kidnappings, extremist attacks, and banditry, fueling public anxiety over the extent of foreign military involvement beyond public view.

Published date: December 01 2025, 04:20

URL: https://businessday.ng/news/article/us-allegedly-preparing-uav-strikes-in-nigeria-as-covert-isr-flights-reported/
Source: Businessday NG
Classification: Politics
Sentiment: neutral
Reporting voice: Investigative
Continent: Africa

</doc>

Title: NLC to hold nationwide protest on December 17 over worsening insecurity

Summary: 
The Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) announced a nationwide protest on December 17, 2025, in response to the deteriorating security situation in Nigeria. The decision followed the abduction of 24 schoolgirls in Kebbi on November 17, during which two staff members were killed. The National Executive Council (NEC) meeting held on December 4, 2025, at the NLC Sub-Secretariat in Yaba, Lagos, resolved to demand an immediate and thorough investigation into, and prosecution of, all individuals involved in the withdrawal of security personnel from affected schools. The NEC expressed deep concern over the surge in kidnappings targeting schoolchildren, particularly in remote and fringe areas, and criticized the government for failing to secure schools adequately. The NEC directed all NLC affiliates and state councils to fully mobilize for the protest. The NEC also addressed broader systemic issues, including chronic underfunding of tertiary education, poor infrastructure, and non-payment of staff entitlements. It warned against government 'divide-and-rule' tactics in union negotiations and called for a fair remuneration structure for academic and non-academic staff. The union expressed concern over the ongoing Joint Health Sector Unions (JOHESU) strike, which began on November 14, 2025, and cautioned that failure to resolve negotiations could lead to NLC-affiliated unions joining the strike. The NEC also ordered the withdrawal of NLC members from committees led by Nenadi Usman and urged the Labour Party to realign with working-class principles, decrying its current state as hijacked and reduced to a political appendage. The NLC warned that failure by the Federal Government to address insecurity and other pressing issues could trigger escalated industrial actions across health, education, and other sectors.

Published date: December 09 2025, 06:36

URL: https://nairametrics.com/2025/12/09/nlc-to-hold-nationwide-protest-on-december-17-over-worsening-insecurity/
Source: Nairametrics
Classification: Politics

Title: US congressman Riley Moore announces roundtable on persecution of Christians in Nigeria

Summary: 
US Congressman Riley Moore announced on X (formerly Twitter) on December 2, 2025, that President Donald Trump had tasked him and members of the House Appropriations Committee with investigating the persecution of Christians in Nigeria. As part of this effort, the committee is hosting a roundtable to gather testimony and inform a comprehensive report directed by the President. The report aims to examine massacres of Nigerian Christians and outline steps Congress could take to support the White House’s global religious protection initiatives. Moore emphasized that the United States would not turn a blind eye to Christians suffering for their faith. This development underscores heightened US congressional engagement on global religious freedom. In November 2025, Trump declared Nigeria a 'Country of Particular Concern' due to alleged mass killings by radical groups, warning of possible US military intervention, including air strikes, if Nigeria failed to act. These claims have sparked diplomatic tensions and sharp rebuttals from Nigerian officials. Prior to the announcement, Moore met with Nuhu Ribadu, Nigeria’s National Security Adviser, and other senior government officials in Washington, D.C., to discuss strengthening US-Nigeria cooperation in combating terrorism and ending violence against Christian communities. Moore stated on X on November 19, 2025: 'I made it crystal clear that the United States must see tangible steps to ensure that Christians are not subject to violence, persecution, displacement, and death simply for believing in our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.'

Published date: December 02 2025, 08:09

URL: https://www.legit.ng/world/1685927-us-congressman-riley-moore-announces-roundtable-persecution-christians-nigeria/
Source: Legit.ng - Nigeria news.
Classification: Politics
Sentiment: neutral
Reporting voice: Objective
Continent: Africa

Title: Full Statement Of US Joint Hearing On Nigeria Insecurity

Summary: 
On December 3, 2025, the U.S. House Foreign Affairs Committee held a joint hearing with the House Appropriations Committee to address the escalating violence and targeted persecution of Christians in Nigeria. The hearing followed President Donald Trump’s October 31, 2024 directive to investigate the killings of Christians in Nigeria. Attendees included key lawmakers such as Rep. Mario Díaz-Balart, Rep. Robert Aderholt, Rep. Riley Moore, Rep. Brian Mast, Rep. Chris Smith, U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom Chair Vicky Hartzler, Alliance Defending Freedom International’s Sean Nelson, and Council on Foreign Relations Fellow Dr. Ebenezer Obadare. Lawmakers emphasized that the violence is not mere 'inter-communal conflict' but a coordinated religious cleansing campaign by groups like Boko Haram, Islamic State West Africa Province, and radicalized Fulani militants, aimed at expelling Christians from Nigeria’s Middle Belt and imposing radical Islamist ideology. Rep. Mast affirmed the U.S. designation of Nigeria as a Country of Particular Concern (CPC), calling for disarmament of militias, return of displaced families, and justice for perpetrators. Rep. Smith condemned the Nigerian government’s complicity and failure to protect citizens, urging swift U.S. action. Expert testimony highlighted a surge in violence: on November 22, 2025, 303 children and 12 teachers were abducted from St. Mary’s School in Niger State; in Kwara State, gunmen attacked a church, killing two and kidnapping several; in Zamfara and Katsina States, over 100 people were abducted from a mosque and 27 worshipers were killed. Hartzler stressed the urgency of U.S. action, calling for improved accountability, early warning systems, police reform, and security assistance. Nelson detailed firsthand accounts of Christians imprisoned on false blasphemy charges, kidnapped, tortured, forced into marriage, and killed—often with no government response. Obadare identified Boko Haram as Nigeria’s primary threat, advocating for U.S. pressure to dismantle the group, abolish Sharia law in northern states, and disband Hisbah enforcement units. The hearing concluded with a call for sustained U.S. diplomatic and security engagement to protect religious minorities and stabilize Nigeria.

Published date: December 03 2025, 07:59

URL: https://www.naijanews.com/2025/12/03/full-statement-of-us-joint-hearing-on-nigeria-insecurity/
Source: Naija News
Classification: Politics
Sentiment: negative
Reporting voice: Analytical
Continent: Africa

</doc>

Title: Nigerian air force strikes putschists in Benin  --  agency

Summary: 
On December 7, 2025, Nigeria's air force conducted airstrikes in Cotonou, the capital of Benin, targeting coup attempters, according to AFP citing a Nigerian air force spokesman, Ehimen Ejodamen. The operation was carried out in accordance with protocols of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) and the regional standby force. The strikes targeted military personnel attempting to flee Cotonou in armored vehicles, as reported by the Nigerian Makama news portal. The attack was authorized by Benin's legitimate government. Witnesses reported multiple explosions across various parts of the city. Earlier that day, Benin's government announced it had foiled a military coup attempt, claiming that President Patrice Talon had been unlawfully removed from office by a group of military personnel. The government stated that it had arrested some of the coup plotters and maintained control over the situation. The incident occurred on Sunday morning, and the government confirmed it had restored order.

Published date: December 07 2025, 21:00

Title: Christian genocide: US military submits plan for possible strike in Nigeria

Summary: 
The U.S. military has reportedly submitted contingency plans for potential strikes in Nigeria, following a directive from President Donald Trump to prepare for possible military action over allegations of Christian genocide. According to a New York Times report published on November 5, 2025, the U.S. Africa Command developed three options—light, medium, and heavy—for a military response, with the 'heavy option' described as the most forceful action the U.S. could take. The plans were submitted to the Department of War as requested by Secretary Pete Hegseth. President Trump designated Nigeria a 'Country of Particular Concern' on November 1, 2025, citing claims of Christians being massacred, and placed the Department of War on red alert, warning that U.S. military strikes would follow if the Nigerian government fails to stop the violence. The report was published by Daily Post Nigeria on November 6, 2025.

Published date: November 06 2025, 07:02
